reason: The only available action adds fuel to the muscle fibers, which may help support their continuing work.
expectation: I expect the fibers to gain a fuel supply; oxygen may still be needed.

effect: Sugar processing produces some ATP and leaves fuel for mitochondria, so adding oxygen seems like the next step toward supporting continued work.
reaction: It is useful to see that some ATP is made outside mitochondria.
reason: Oxygen is the only offered combination and may help the mitochondria use the processed fuel.
expectation: I expect the fibers to use oxygen to support further ATP production, though I am unsure exactly how the game will represent it.

effect: Oxygen helps the fibers replenish ATP from fuel, supporting their pulling machinery. The next goal is to organize the fibers into muscles.
reaction: The distinction that oxygen enables fuel use rather than providing energy is useful.
reason: Wrapping the supported fibers is the only offered combination and seems like a way to organize them into muscle groups.
expectation: I expect the wrapping to bundle the fibers into a muscle structure, though I am unsure how the two opposing groups will be formed.

effect: The wrapping bundles the fibers and passes their tension toward the muscle ends, so tendons may connect that pull to the framework.
reaction: The connection between supporting material and transmitting tension is useful.
reason: I’ll add the front tendons to begin forming one of the opposing muscle groups.
expectation: I expect a front muscle group with tendons that can transmit its pull, though I don’t yet know how it will attach.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons also seem useful, but either group looks like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The front tendons form bending muscles that can pull on bones once the framework is arranged. The rear tendons appear to form the opposing group.
reaction: It is useful to see how tendon placement relates to bending the elbow.
reason: The rear tendons are the only offered combination and should help complete the opposing muscle groups.
expectation: I expect a muscle group that can straighten the elbow when attached on the appropriate side.

effect: The rear tendons formed straightening muscles, completing the opposing pair. Both groups still need the right attachments to move a joint.
reaction: The paired pulls make sense, though the framework remains unfinished.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile because the result connected fuel use and ATP replenishment to the muscle's pulling machinery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the rear tendons felt repetitive after forming the bending muscles, although it completed the opposing pair.

surprise.text: I was interested that sugar processing makes some ATP outside mitochondria and leaves partly processed fuel for them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, though the menu showed compatible combinations, so I did not have to work out which parts fit.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the opposing muscles attach to a framework and move the joint.
